notes: Implements slash-remember and slash-kb commands (src/bot/handlers/commands.py) and the adm_kb admin sub-router (new src/bot/handlers/admin_kb.py plus keyboards/admin_kb.py), plus supporting plumbing: kb_organizer_ids added to chat_settings write-allowlist (A3 deferred this to A4); new FSM state for the add-organizer reply flow; new admin main-menu entry; router registration. Deliberate, documented deviation from G2's copy register: G2's admin submenu contract had no chat-id parameter, which is non-functional against ADR-0003's per-chat schema (kb_enabled and kb_organizer_ids are columns on chat_settings, scoped per chat). Added a chat-picker step first, reusing the existing whitelist chat-list pagination pattern, before the per-chat submenu. Rationale documented in admin_kb.py's module docstring and the commit message. Callback-data worst case stays well under the 64-byte Telegram budget. Remember-command gates on kb_enabled plus sender being bot admin (authority rank 4) or a chat KB organizer (authority rank 3); embeds fact text via the AI router before writing the fact (mirrors the existing RAG memory store pattern). KB-view command is public with no gating, group mode is terse (no predicate or provenance shown), DM mode is bold-title topic-sectioned with provenance and dd.mm.yyyy dates, per the copy register. Organizer-add resolves only via a forwarded message (a concrete user id); a plain at-username with no forward has no chat-scoped lookup path in Phase 1 and falls through to the existing not-found copy rather than faking a match -- flagged as a known gap. Display-name resolution uses a Telegram API lookup with a fallback on failure, matching the existing fallback precedent already used elsewhere for chat titles. Organizer-id list reads and writes use JSON serialization with defensive parsing on read, matching the existing pattern used for other JSONB columns in this codebase. Two gaps in the designer's copy register were filled with minimal own-voice strings not previously decided by design: the remember-command's kb-disabled and permission-denied messages, and the chat-picker screen title -- recommend folding these back into the copy register doc. Routing hints for qa: needs end-to-end coverage for the admin FSM add-organizer flow through a real dispatcher (this item's tests call handlers directly), for the Telegram API failure fallback paths, and for the embedding-failure-but-fact-still-saved path (fact is saved with a null embedding and won't be retrievable by vector search until re-saved -- worth an explicit test and possibly a user-facing warning).
